ROLE SUMMARY:

The Global Operation Services Center (GOSC) is seeking a highly motivated Manager, Incentive Compensation Design to lead incentive compensation strategy and design for Pfizer's Tier 3 International Markets. In this role, you will partner directly with business leaders across diverse global markets to develop bonus plans, quota-setting methodologies, and recognition programs that motivate customer-facing colleagues and drive business performance.

You will serve as a trusted advisor, translating business objectives into incentive compensation solutions that are simple, motivating, fiscally responsible, and compliant with Pfizer policies and governance standards. Working closely with the GOSC Delivery team, you will also lead the successful implementation and ongoing administration of these programs.

This role combines strategic consulting, analytics, and stakeholder management. It is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of data and business strategy, enjoys solving complex performance challenges, and can confidently communicate recommendations to senior leaders. Success in this position requires both strong quantitative capabilities and the ability to influence decision-making through clear, evidence-based insights.

Beyond supporting assigned markets, this role will contribute to broader GOSC strategic initiatives, driving innovation, continuous improvement, and best practices across international incentive compensation programs.

ROLE RESPOSNSIBILITIES:

Incentive Compensation Strategy & Design

• Design, enhance, and maintain incentive compensation plans aligned with local business strategies and commercial objectives.
• Develop and refine quota-setting methodologies that support performance, fairness, and business growth.
• Design local recognition and award programs that reinforce desired behaviors and strategic priorities.
• Partner with business leaders to identify challenges and proactively recommend incentive compensation solutions.

Analytics & Strategic Consulting

• Analyze incentive compensation program effectiveness and identify opportunities for optimization.
• Leverage data and analytics to generate insights, evaluate program performance, and support strategic decision-making.
• Build robust business cases and recommendations for plan design changes, balancing motivation, affordability, and risk management.
• Serve as a trusted advisor to market leadership by providing objective, data-driven guidance.

Stakeholder Partnership

• Develop strong relationships with market leaders and gain deep understanding of local business priorities, products, customer dynamics, and competitive landscapes.
• Facilitate discussions and influence stakeholders through credible recommendations and clear communication.
• Collaborate effectively across Commercial Excellence, Finance, PX, Compliance, and other partner functions.

Program Implementation, Governance & Service Delivery

• Partner with GOSC Delivery teams to ensure timely, accurate, and effective implementation and administration of incentive compensation programs.
• Collaborate with GOSC to calculate bonus payouts, contests, awards, and field quotas using approved processes, tools, and templates.
• Ensure all incentive compensation deliverables are accurate, complete, and distributed to the field force according to established timelines.
• Own governance and operational oversight across all incentive compensation services within assigned markets.
• Create, maintain, and manage incentive compensation production calendars, ensuring alignment across business, operational, and support stakeholders.
• Hold stakeholders accountable for data ownership, validation, quality, and timely submission of required inputs.
• Implement new processes, tools, and initiatives in alignment with regional and global standards, guidelines, and strategic priorities.
• Maintain audit readiness through accurate documentation, record retention, and archiving practices in partnership with GOSC.
• Ensure adherence to all relevant incentive compensation policies, procedures, governance requirements, and Legal and Compliance standards, including GMIS policy application.

Analytics & Strategic Consulting

• Analyze incentive compensation program effectiveness and identify opportunities for optimization.
• Generate, maintain, and communicate incentive compensation analyses, reports, dashboards, and insights to monitor program health and support business decision-making.
• Leverage data and analytics to identify trends, evaluate program performance, and recommend improvements aligned with market objectives.
• Build robust business cases for compensation plan and quota-setting enhancements, balancing motivation, affordability, and compliance.
• Serve as a trusted advisor to market leadership by providing objective, data-driven recommendations and solutions.

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

• Lead strategic projects and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance GOSC's value proposition, service delivery, and operational effectiveness.
• Proactively identify business needs and opportunities to improve existing services, processes, tools, and incentive compensation programs.
• Drive the adoption of best practices, innovation, and standardization across supported international markets.
• Work independently and lead by influence, delivering on business strategies, goals, and objectives through strong analytical, facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

Key Success Factors

The successful candidate will:

• Demonstrate a strong balance of analytical rigor, business acumen, and stakeholder influence.
• Be equally comfortable developing complex incentive compensation models and presenting recommendations to senior business leaders.
• Operate with a high degree of ownership, accountability, and independent judgment.
• Effectively manage multiple priorities across diverse international markets while maintaining attention to detail and execution excellence.
• Build trust through data-driven decision making, collaboration, and consistent delivery of high-quality results.
• Champion continuous improvement and proactively identify opportunities to enhance business value.

QUALIFICATION:

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Data Science, Operations Research, Business Analytics, Economics, Finance, or a related quantitative discipline. An MBA or other advanced degree is preferred.

• Proven ability to manage complex operational timelines, coordinate tasks across multiple stakeholders, and ensure delivery against critical business deadlines.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with experience translating complex data into actionable business insights and recommendations.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. KKR’s insurance subsidiaries offer retirement, life and reinsurance products under the management of Global Atlantic Financial Group. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries.

K-STAR INVESTMENT SERVICES OVERVIEW

K-Star Asset Management LLC ("K-Star") was formed in 2022 and is a wholly owned subsidiary of KKR. K- Star Investment Services supports the risk management of its Asset-Based Finance investments, asset management, securities investing, and client experience for its Real Estate Credit franchise as both verticals continue to scale. The K-Star team includes industry specialists to oversee residential mortgage investments, consumer finance investments, special servicing, stabilized and transitional loan asset management across many KKR investment portfolios.

POSITION SUMMARY

K-Star is seeking a detail-oriented and analytically rigorous Credit & Valuations Associate to join our residential mortgage whole loan acquisition team. In this dual-function role, you will serve as a key contributor to both the valuation and credit review processes that underpin our secondary market acquisition strategy. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in residential appraisal review and mortgage credit underwriting, with the ability to develop scalable processes and serve as a subject matter expert for the broader team. The role is based in Dallas and collaborates regularly with the deal team at KKR.

We are passionate about operational excellence and providing our investment and business operations colleagues the ability to seamlessly execute liquid and private credit investments around the globe. We are committed to continuous improvement, both in the operations we perform and in the environment in which we work. We work in collaborative teams within the context and support of a large, global investment firm. We can offer challenging and rewarding work and opportunities for career advancement and learning in both the business and operational spheres.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Perform detailed appraisal reviews on residential mortgage loans, evaluating for accuracy, reasonableness, current market trends, and overall property condition
• Develop a tiered process flow for utilizing third-party valuation tools (AVMs, BPOs, desktop appraisals) to support and corroborate review conclusions
• Provide clear, well-documented review commentary and actionable recommendations to support acquisition decisions
• Create and implement a systemic procedure for the continued review of supplemental valuations obtained by loan servicing to ensure ongoing accuracy and compliance
• Serve as the primary knowledge source on the team for all appraisal-related activity, market dynamics, and evolving industry standards
• Review originator underwriting guidelines for variations across counterparties and collaborate with third-party vendors to create a consolidated framework that highlights key differences across guidelines
• Maintain current and historical versions of originator underwriting guidelines, and track the specific guideline version under which individual loans were originated
• Monitor and analyze trends across underwriting guidelines to proactively identify shifts in market standards and lending practices
• Aid in reviewing credit diligence results, identifying compensating factors, and documenting exceptions for new loan acquisitions

QUALIFCATIONS

• Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree
• Strong working knowledge of residential appraisal methodologies, including the cost, sales comparison, and income approaches to value
• Demonstrated experience reviewing Uniform Residential Appraisal Reports (URARs), Broker Price Opinions (BPOs), and Automated Valuation Models (AVMs)
• Thorough understanding of evolving appraisal regulations (USPAP, Dodd-Frank, GSE requirements) and secondary market valuation trends
• Deep understanding of residential mortgage credit underwriting standards and key performance metrics (DTI, LTV, FICO, reserves, etc.)
• Familiarity with conventional, business purpose (DSCR, fix-and-flip), and non-QM lending requirements and their respective risk profiles
• Hands-on experience in secondary market operations, post-close quality control, or investor-level loan review
• 4–5+ years of progressive experience in residential mortgage whole loan valuations, operations, and/or acquisition diligence
• Versatile, innovative, and analytical professional who is a critical thinker with the ability to synthesize complex data into clear conclusions
• Excellent attention to detail with strong organizational skills and effective time management in a fast-paced environment
• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present findings, collaborate cross-functionally, and perform effectively in a deadline-driven environment
• Knowledge of the loan acquisition process, warehouse lending, loan securitization, and servicing transfers is a plus
• Proficiency with industry-standard appraisal and credit platforms (e.g., Collateral Analytics, Clear Capital, CoreLogic, Black Knight)
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills including data analysis, pivot tables, and scenario modeling
• Experience working with loan-level data tapes and due diligence platforms
• Familiarity with regulatory frameworks governing residential mortgage lending and secondary market transactions

Are you ready to shape the future of Amazon's digital services distribution through strategic financial leadership? Amazon Fuse & Mobile Business Development (MBD) Finance Team is seeking an innovative finance professional with exceptional analytical skills and business judgment to accelerate Amazon's growth through partnerships with Mobile Operators, video distributors, and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) worldwide. This high-impact role focuses on supporting some of Amazon's most strategic commercial partnerships in India and Asia Pacific, where you'll build complex financial models, quantify customer value, and influence senior leadership decisions.

As a key finance partner, you'll work at the intersection of finance, business development, and marketing, transforming complex datasets into actionable insights that drive Amazon's flywheel. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop rigorous analysis, challenge business assumptions, and deliver recommendations that shape multi-million dollar partnerships. This is a unique opportunity to join a centralized corporate business development team where your financial expertise will directly impact how millions of customers access Amazon's digital services globally.

Key job responsibilities
- Build complex, scalable, and flexible financial models to evaluate partnership opportunities, interpret data, and deliver recommendations that drive results and influence leaders throughout Amazon
- Develop and report key input metrics that support business growth, transforming complex datasets into actionable insights for decision-making on strategic partnerships
- Partner with business development and marketing teams to challenge business assumptions, evaluate partnership economics, and provide thought leadership in quantifying the value of distinct customer behaviors
- Collaborate with finance leaders and Business Intelligence teams to enhance and automate financial reports for business reviews, ensuring accuracy in billing, cost allocation, and financial presentations
- Communicate financial strategies and analysis to VP level leaders, effectively influencing stakeholders across a matrixed environment while navigating ambiguity in uncharted territory

A day in the life
You'll start your day analyzing the financial performance of strategic partnerships across India and Asia Pacific, diving deep into partner economics and customer metrics. You'll build sophisticated financial models to evaluate new partnership opportunities with mobile operators or video distributors, then jump into collaborative sessions with business development teams to challenge assumptions and refine deal structures. Throughout the day, you'll work with Business Intelligence teams to automate reporting dashboards, conduct industry research on potential partners, and prepare compelling financial narratives for senior leadership reviews. You'll balance rigorous financial analysis with creative problem-solving, constantly seeking opportunities to advance Amazon's growth initiatives.

About the team
The Amazon Fuse & Mobile Business Development (MBD) Finance Team is a small, tight-knit group of analytical and creative professionals working on strategic partnerships that accelerate Amazon's flywheel by distributing digital services globally. This centralized corporate business development team partners with Mobile Operators, Multi-channel Video Programming Distributors (MVPDs), and OEMs worldwide to bring Amazon's digital services to millions of customers.

The team values first-principles thinkers who thrive in fast-paced, constantly evolving environments. You'll work alongside finance professionals who combine rigorous analytical skills with business creativity, diving deep into complex problems while remaining adaptable and action-oriented. The team's mission is to provide thoughtful financial leadership that directly influences senior leaders' decision-making on some of Amazon's most impactful commercial partnerships, with a particular focus on high-growth markets in India and Asia Pacific.

jobs.description: At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. About Lilly At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, and in Mexico we have been making medicines since 1908. Driven by our enduring values of Integrity, Excellence, and Respect for People , we put people first — in our labs, in our communities, and in our workplaces. The Opportunity Neuroscience is one of Lilly’s most enduring scientific commitments, and Alzheimer’s disease is among the fastest-moving fields in medicine — moving from symptomatic management toward biologically confirmed diagnosis, earlier detection, and intervention in the early symptomatic stages of disease. As a Medical Science Liaison (MSL) , you will be a credible, field-based scientific partner: translating complex evidence into clinical practice, building trust-based relationships with healthcare experts, and generating the insights that shape Lilly’s medical strategy in México — in a therapeutic area where the diagnostic pathway itself must be strengthened alongside the science. What You Will Do Scientific Knowledge & Communication Maintain expert command of the evidence across Alzheimer’s disease and the wider neurodegeneration landscape — amyloid and tau biology, fluid and imaging biomarkers, cognitive and functional endpoints, and Lilly’s current and pipeline neuroscience assets , engaging on investigational assets only in a reactive, compliant manner. Translate clinical trial data, real-world evidence, HEOR outputs, and updates to diagnostic criteria and clinical guidance (NIA-AA, IWG, AAN, Alzheimer’s Association appropriate-use recommendations, Academia Mexicana de Neurología) into clear, balanced, guideline-aligned scientific narratives. Discuss safety and monitoring considerations for this class of therapies — including imaging surveillance requirements and patient risk-stratification — with the balance and rigor the topic demands. Respond to unsolicited scientific inquiries with rigorous, non-promotional, evidence-based information. Customer Engagement & Scientific Exchange Map, prioritize, and build trust-based partnerships with scientific and clinical experts across neurology, cognitive and behavioral neurology, geriatrics, psychiatry, neuroradiology and nuclear medicine, neuropsychology, internal medicine, and primary care — recognizing that Alzheimer’s care depends on a diagnostic and treatment chain rather than on a single prescriber. Engage the wider care team whose readiness determines whether evidence reaches patients — neuropsychology, imaging and infusion services, nursing, laboratory, and hospital administration colleagues. Deliver high-impact scientific presentations to HCPs and multidisciplinary care teams, and provide scientific support at national and international congresses. Engage private and public stakeholders (IMSS, ISSSTE, CCINSHAE — including INNN and INGER — COFEPRIS, CENETEC, CSG, SEDENA, SEMAR, PEMEX) in compliant, non-promotional scientific exchange that supports access decisions grounded in evidence. Diagnostic Pathway & Health-System Readiness Characterize the local diagnostic pathway end to end — cognitive screening, specialist referral, biomarker confirmation, imaging access and reporting capacity, and treatment-monitoring infrastructure — and identify where it breaks down. Support scientific education that strengthens diagnostic confidence and appropriate patient identification, including disease staging, differential diagnosis, and interpretation of biomarker results. Partner with institutions to understand the capabilities they require to deliver and monitor therapies in this class, and feed that intelligence into medical and cross-functional readiness planning. Territory Ownership & Insight Generation Own the medical profile of your assigned territory: define engagement priorities, uncover clinical care gaps, and capture actionable insights that inform medical, evidence-generation, and launch plans. Map centers of excellence and emerging referral networks, recognizing that Alzheimer’s diagnostic and treatment capability in México is concentrated in a limited number of institutions with markedly different levels of readiness. Support investigator-initiated trials, real-world evidence projects, registries, and publication activities in partnership with the broader Medical Affairs team. Strategic Vision & Cross-Functional Leadership Partner with Access, HEOR, Regulatory, Commercial, Marketing, and Compliance colleagues so Medical Affairs contributes as a strategic, evidence-based voice across the full product lifecycle — pre-launch, launch, and post-launch. Contribute to the broader dementia-care conversation in México — with scientific societies, academic institutions, and patient and caregiver organizations — in a strictly non-promotional capacity. Uphold Lilly’s zero-tolerance ethics culture and ensure every activity meets Lilly global standards. What You Will Bring Education & Experience (either path works) Advanced degree in health sciences (MD, PharmD, PhD, or MSc) with at least 2 years of clinical, research, industry, or Medical Affairs experience — training or practice in neurology, geriatrics, psychiatry, or neuroscience is a strong advantage, OR Bachelor’s degree in life sciences with 5+ years of relevant clinical, research, or pharmaceutical industry experience in a therapeutic area related to neuroscience or neurodegenerative disease. Core Capabilities Fluent English and Spanish, able to present complex scientific data and manage rigorous Q&A in both languages. Demonstrated ability to communicate scientific evidence clearly to diverse audiences, build trusted multidisciplinary relationships, and translate qualitative field interactions into strategic insights. Comfort with quantitative and imaging-based evidence — cognitive and functional rating scales, biomarker assays, and neuroimaging concepts — and the ability to discuss uncertainty and clinical meaningfulness honestly. Digital fluency — comfort operating within CRM ecosystems (Veeva CRM), literature databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, UpToDate, ClinicalKey), virtual-engagement platforms (MS Teams), and insight/analytics dashboards; openness to AI-enabled internal tools that enhance medical affairs productivity. Mobility — willing and able to travel approximately 50–60% nationally , including overnight, complemented by a parallel omnichannel engagement model for virtual interactions. What Will Help You Stand Out Working knowledge of Alzheimer’s diagnostic and outcome tools — cognitive and functional instruments (MMSE, MoCA, CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog, ADCS-ADL), CSF and plasma biomarkers, and amyloid or tau PET imaging. Practical knowledge of COFEPRIS, CSG, and the Compendio Nacional de Insumos para la Salud (CNIS) processes, with contribution to value dossiers or payer-engagement activities. Experience supporting the build-out of specialized care pathways, site readiness, or complex-therapy delivery models in a hospital or institutional setting. Hands-on involvement in real-world evidence projects, investigator-initiated trials, disease registries, or peer-reviewed publications. Experience with omnichannel and digital engagement (virtual advisory boards, asynchronous expert platforms, analytics dashboards). Active participation in Mexican scientific societies (Academia Mexicana de Neurología, Sociedad Mexicana de Neurología y Psiquiatría, Asociación Mexicana de Gerontología y Geriatría) or in dementia-focused patient and caregiver organizations. Leadership in diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives, or peer mentoring within Medical Affairs. How You Will Grow Lilly Mexico is deeply committed to developing its people: 90% of leadership positions are filled by colleagues whose careers have been developed internally, and 44% of these leaders are Latin American talent . As an MSL you will have structured development pathways across Medical Affairs, access to Lilly’s global scientific networks, and exposure to one of the industry’s most sustained research commitments in neurodegeneration. Our Commitment to Inclusion We believe every person should feel welcomed, valued, and heard. Our Employee Resource Groups — including OLA (Organization of Latinx at Lilly) and WILL (Women’s Initiative for Leading at Lilly) — reflect our commitment to building a team as diverse as the patients we serve.
